title: private-deploy-field-scratchpad
content:
Personal scratchpad - Private deploys (VPC / on-prem)
Quick notes, checklist, blockers + env reminders. Mostly for on-site installs + customer prep.

---
2026-02-25 (latest updates)
- Customer: AcmeInsure (POC) — on-prem (air-gapped) in their Azure Stack.
- Primary blocker: KMS integration requires HSM cert rotation policy that customer enforces (their HSM rotates certs every 30 days). Need to handle key metadata re-attach without downtime.
- Action: PR #88 (private-deploy-scripts) has hot-reload for KMS creds but needs GH review + integration test against mock HSM. Assigned to Priya.

TODO (short):
- [ ] finish integration test for HSM hot-reload (Priya)
- [x] produce pre-install checklist for Acme (network/firewall/ips) - done 2026-02-20
- [ ] schedule runbook review with SRE (Diego)
- [ ] confirm backup/restore of DB snapshots works with our restore tool (on-prem)
- [ ] validate cert chain compatibility for Envoy mTLS across their appliance

Pre-install network notes for customer (copy to email):
- Allow outbound to these endpoints (if not fully air-gapped):
  - installer.redwood.ai:443 (initial bootstrap)
  - packages.redwood.internal.s3.amazonaws.com:443 (container pull proxy)
  - metrics.redwood.ai:443 (optional, for console)
- If fully air-gapped, we will provide tarball bundle + installer image (deliver via secure courier).
- Required ports (internal):
  - 8443 (control-plane API)
  - 6379 (local redis for cache) - we recommend Redis be clustered for production
  - 2379-2380 (etcd) - locked to control-plane nodes only
  - 10250 (kubelet) - if customer runs our k8s operators

Environment & infra reminders:
- Default service CIDR: 10.96.0.0/12 (but customer uses 10.0.0.0/8 in parts) — check overlap.
- Node IPs must be static for GPU nodes (NVIDIA licensing + driver stability).
- GPU driver matrix: use nvidia-driver-525 for Ampere customers (we validated on their node), 535 for Hopper if they have newer cards. Put exact driver version in installer manifest.
- Kernel version: RHEL 8.6 preferred; we saw regressions on 9.2 in internal tests (OOM during compilation).

Installer steps (high level, notes-to-self):
1) Validate preflight (run ./rdw-preflight.sh) — checks: disk, kernel, IP, firewall, docker/containerd version, swap disabled, KMS reachability.
2) Upload bundle (if air-gapped) or configure bootstrap token for online install.
3) Apply network policy (CNI: calico default) -> set MTU 1450 for Azure Stack overlay.
4) Deploy control-plane components (etcd -> control-plane -> api -> operator). Watch for etcd quorum.
5) GPU node join (install drivers via our daemonset) -> verify nvidia-smi visible.
6) Deploy redis and local caching layer -> ensure persistence path on SSD.
7) Bring up serving runtime, set model-store path (NFS recommended) -> note: customer's NFS uses export options root_squash; we mount with fsGroup workaround.
8) Configure KMS plugin: load key-mapping file -> run key-attach job -> verify that sealed secrets decrypt.

Common troubleshooting notes (from prior installs):
- etcd kept restarting if clock skew > 2s across nodes; remind customer to enable chrony and validate drift.
- Kernel module mismatch: make sure /lib/modules matches running kernel before installing nvidia-driver.
- Docker vs containerd: installer prefers containerd; if docker present, recommend removal or isolated runtime class.
- SELinux: enforce causes permission denials on our operator's init containers (we ship a policy but still ask customers to test).

Quick commands I run locally during install:
- ./rdw-preflight.sh --target acme --output preflight-acme.log
- kubectl -n redwood get pods -o wide --sort-by=.status.startTime
- journalctl -u kubelet -f | grep -i nvidia
- etcdctl --endpoints=https://10.0.5.11:2379 member list --cert=etc/etcd-peer.crt --key=etc/etcd-peer.key

Notes about secrets & rotation:
- We support two KMS modes: remote-KMS (managed HSM, via customer network) and local-hsm (on-prem HSM appliance). For remote-KMS, we need outbound 443 to KMS endpoint + client cert.
- If customer rotates HSM certs frequently (Acme), we need to ensure our key meta mapping persists and rotation job re-attaches keys to runtime without restart. Current code attempts reattach but sometimes fails if mapping file changed.
- Short-term workaround: schedule a small maintenance window and run key-reattach script (scripts/attach-keys.sh) then restart only the operator (not serving pods).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Confirm whether Acme's firewall allows egress to our metrics endpoint or whether they will require an on-prem metrics aggregator. If yes, deploy statsd->prom gateway. (Ask CS)
- Does Acme require FIPS-compliant TLS stacks? If so, we need to enable FIPS builds for envoy and openssl (impact on perf).
- Need to add a test case to CI that simulates HSM rotating certs every 30 days.

Meeting notes (quick):
- 2026-02-18 call with Acme infra: they will provide HSM test instance + route table tomorrow. They prefer air-gapped approach but will allow limited egress for bootstrap.
- Ask: what is their SSH bastion IP range? We'll add to preflight allowlist.

Copy-paste checklist for on-site engineer:
- [ ] Confirm physical rack space + PDUs labeled
- [ ] Verify out-of-band console access (ILO / iDRAC)
- [ ] Confirm time sync across nodes
- [ ] Bring USB installer bundle and signing key (if air-gapped)
- [ ] Bring spare SATA SSDs (for db restore)

Random notes to self:
- If model-store NFS is slow, enable local cache layer (redis-backed) and set model prefetch to 2 concurrently.
- For large models, verify swap is disabled and file ulimit is >= 65536.

End of scratchpad.

(Formatting intentionally messy — this is a quick personal log. Move to Confluence once stable.)
